title: Best Months for a Turkish Blue Cruise Gulet Charter: Sea & Wind Guide
seoTitle: Best Month for a Gulet Cruise in Turkey: Sea & Wind Guide
metaDescription: Compare May–October for a gulet cruise in Turkey. See Meltemi wind timing along Bodrum and Datça, sea temperatures, and monthly charter rate shifts.
quickAnswer: The best month for a gulet cruise in Turkey is June or September, when sea temperatures sit around 23–26°C, bays are noticeably quieter than August, and weekly charter rates drop 20–35% below peak summer. May and October offer cooler evenings and maximum value, while July–August bring peak heat and stronger afternoon Meltemi winds.

body.text: At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), our two founders advise international families and private groups on independent, client-paid, flat-fee itineraries across Türkiye. Paid by our clients. Independent of provider commissions.
How do May–June, July–August and September–October compare for sailing?

May–June brings lush green hillsides, long daylight hours, and warming waters (20–24°C); July–August delivers peak heat, crowded anchorages, and active afternoon winds; and September–October offers the warmest sea temperatures of the year (24–26°C in September) paired with calm coves and softer afternoon light.

Traditional wooden gulets operate primarily out of [Bodrum, Marmaris, Göcek, and Fethiye](https://goturkiye.com/aegean/blue-voyage), cruising protected waters such as the [Gulf of Gökova](https://goturkiye.com/bluevoyage/turkish-gulets) and the Hisarönü Gulf. According to the [Turkish State Meteorological Service (MGM) July 2026 climate report](https://www.mgm.gov.tr/eng/Monthly-Climate/2026/State_of_the_Climate_in_July_2026.pdf), Aegean coastal mean temperatures reach roughly 26.5–27.0°C in July, with daytime highs frequently climbing past 34°C around Bodrum and Datça.
When is Meltemi wind strongest along the Bodrum and Datça coasts?

The northerly Meltemi (Etesian) wind blows strongest from late June through late August, peaking in afternoon gusts along exposed stretches of the Bodrum Peninsula, Knidos Cape, and the outer Datça coast. Mornings typically remain glassy for swimming, while winds build between 13:00 and 18:00 before dropping at dusk.

As veteran [Bodrum Blue Voyage operators note](https://barbarosyachting.com/blue-voyage/bodrum), experienced captains route July–August charters inside the deep, pine-ringed coves of the Gulf of Gökova or shift south toward Göcek and Fethiye's sheltered 12 Islands, where mountain ridges block heavy chop. If anyone in your group is prone to seasickness, choosing a Göcek–Kekova itinerary in peak summer avoids the choppier Bodrum–Datça crossings.
Why do repeat charterers prefer late May, June and September?

Repeat Blue Cruise guests overwhelmingly choose late May, June, and September because you can sleep comfortably in air-conditioned or open-deck cabins without oppressive overnight humidity, anchor in uncrowded bays, and walk coastal ruins like Knidos or Kaunos without midday heat exhaustion.

In peak August, popular coves around Göcek and Bodrum fill with yachts and day boats by noon, and marinas charge peak berthing surcharges. Shoulder-season weeks give your captain freedom to linger in quiet coves. Use this charter planning checklist before signing a contract:

items: Confirm A/C generator hours in writing: Standard gulets often run air conditioning 4–8 hours per day; luxury vessels offer 24-hour silent A/C.
Clarify APA (Advance Provisioning Allowance) vs. full-board menus: Understand exactly what fuel, marina fees, food, and drinks cost before wire transfer.
Match route to wind exposure: Pick Gökova or Hisarönü for classic Bodrum–Datça scenery, or Göcek–Fethiye for the calmest water.
Verify Turkish vs. Greek island transit fees: Adding Symi or Kos adds customs clearance charges and port taxes.
Vet crew and vessel independently: Because we take zero broker kickbacks, [our founders](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/about) help compare specifications objectively.

body.text: How do weekly gulet rates vary by month?

Weekly private gulet charter rates typically follow a three-tier pricing calendar: May and October represent the lowest base rate, June and September run roughly 20–30% higher, and July–August peak at 40–65% above low-season prices for the exact same yacht and crew.

For example, a well-maintained 4-to-5-cabin wooden gulet might charter for €12,000–€16,000 per week in May or October, €16,000–€21,000 in June or September, and €20,000–€28,000+ in July and August (excluding provisions, fuel surcharges, and crew gratuity). Booking a Saturday-to-Saturday week in mid-June or mid-September captures summer swimming conditions while saving thousands of euros. If you are pairing coastal recovery time after an appointment in Istanbul, see our [medical travel planning page](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism) regarding sun and swimming restrictions.

faq.q: What is the warmest month for swimming on a Turkish gulet cruise?
faq.a: August and September have the warmest sea temperatures along the Aegean and Mediterranean coasts, averaging 25–28°C.

faq.q: Can you charter a private gulet for fewer than seven nights?
faq.a: Most private gulets operate Saturday-to-Saturday for seven nights during June–September. Shorter 3- or 4-night charters are occasionally accepted in May or October.

faq.q: Which departure port is best for a first-time Blue Cruise: Bodrum, Marmaris, or Göcek?
faq.a: Göcek and Fethiye offer the shortest airport transfer (25–50 minutes from Dalaman DLM) and the calmest sheltered bays; Bodrum suits travelers wanting historic harbors and classic Gulf of Gökova routes.

faq.q: Do gulets actually sail, or do they mostly motor?
faq.a: Most gulets are motor-sailors that cruise between coves under engine power and hoist sails when afternoon winds—like a steady Meltemi—match the route direction.

faq.q: When should we book a June or September gulet charter?
faq.a: For top-tier 4-to-6-cabin vessels with strong crews, book 6 to 9 months in advance, especially if your dates overlap with [Kurban Bayramı (May 27–30, 2026)](https://vakithesaplama.diyanet.gov.tr/dinigunler.php?yil=2026).
